packet.headline_seed: San Francisco’s housing market has lost its mind
packet.description_seed: The invisible force behind all of this is no mystery to anyone paying attention to the city's tech economy. San Francisco is home to some of the most valuable private companies in the world, and their employees have been quietly accumulating — and, increasingly, cashing out — fortunes.

what: San Francisco’s housing market has lost its mind

clean_source_blocks.text: The invisible force behind all of this is no mystery to anyone paying attention to the city's tech economy. San Francisco is home to some of the most valuable private companies in the world, and their employees have been quietly accumulating — and, increasingly, cashing out — fortunes.

Residential News » San Francisco Edition | By Michael Gerrity | May 5, 2026 4:57 AM ET San Francisco's luxury housing market is staging a powerful comeback--one increasingly defined by the rise of artificial intelligence and the wealth it is generating, according to new data from Redfin. Sales of high-end homes in San Francisco climbed 22.2% in March 2026 from a year earlier, the fifth consecutive month of double-digit gains and among the strongest increases across major U.S. metros. By contrast, non-luxury sales rose just 3.8%, underscoring a widening gap in demand.

San Francisco was written off as tech workers were laid off and remote work became the norm. Then came the robots — and with them, a real estate revival nobody saw coming. Since OpenAI unleashed GPT-3.5 on the world in November 2022, home prices in the Bay Area’s wealthiest ZIP codes have rocketed 13.4%, more than twice the gains posted by the next tier down, according to a Redfin analysis. The city that skeptics were eulogizing is suddenly one of the hottest luxury property markets in the country. The engine behind it is simple: artificial intelligence has become the most lucrative industry on Earth, and its heart beats in Silicon Valley. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind and a wave of heavily-backed startups are all headquartered within miles of each other, and they are paying their talent accordingly.

Redfin Premier agent Ali Mafi has watched the frenzy up close. “There has been an influx of AI companies opening up shop and they’re giving employees giant compensation packages,” he said. “Some people are getting $1 million bonuses. Homes are getting dozens of offers, which is driving up prices and causing many to sell for hundreds of thousands of dollars over the list price. It’s reminiscent of 2020.” That comparison to the pandemic buying frenzy is telling. Back then, rock-bottom mortgage rates sent prices soaring uniformly across all price points, with gains running close to 20% across every market segment.

San Francisco real estate has never been very accessible. But the record sales happening right now in the city’s high-end market are testing the upper limits of what even this famously unaffordable city thought was possible.

Consider a six-bedroom, 5,700-square-foot home in Cow Hollow, one of San Francisco’s most coveted neighborhoods. It was listed two weeks ago at $7.95 million, so, not cheap. It just sold for $15 million. The sellers, who bought the property for $7.8 million in the summer of 2020 as the pandemic was pushing residents out of cities, nearly doubled their money in under five years.

Homes are getting dozens of offers, which is driving up prices and causing many to sell for hundreds of thousands of dollars over the list price. It’s reminiscent of 2020.”

That comparison to the pandemic buying frenzy is telling. Back then, rock-bottom mortgage rates sent prices soaring uniformly across all price points, with gains running close to 20% across every market segment.

Residential News » San Francisco Edition | By Michael Gerrity | May  5, 2026  4:57 AM ET

San Francisco's luxury housing market is staging a powerful comeback--one increasingly defined by the rise of artificial intelligence and the wealth it is generating, according to new data from Redfin.

The rapid expansion of firms such as OpenAI and Anthropic has created a new class of ultra-high-earning buyers, many of whom are channeling unprecedented compensation packages into real estate.

That influx of capital is translating directly into price growth. The median luxury home sold for $6.81 million in March, up 9% from a year earlier and the highest level ever recorded for this time of year, according to Redfin. Prices for non-luxury homes were effectively flat.

Luxury homes went under contract in just 12 days on average--down sharply from 28 days a year earlier and the fastest pace among the largest U.S. cities. Nearly two-thirds of high-end homes sold within two weeks, the highest share in more than a decade.

The resurgence marks a sharp reversal from pandemic-era fears that San Francisco's housing market faced a prolonged decline as residents decamped for lower-cost regions. Instead, AI has reshaped the city's economic foundation, pulling talent--and wealth--back in.

Inventory constraints are amplifying the effect. The number of luxury homes for sale fell more than 15% from a year earlier, extending a multi-year contraction in supply. payload.title: Tekoälyraha kuumentaa San Franciscon luksusasuntomarkkinaa
payload.summary: San Franciscon kalliiden asuntojen kysyntä on vahvistunut nopeasti tekoäly-yhtiöiden synnyttämän varallisuuden vauhdittamana. Redfinin tietojen mukaan luksusasuntojen myynti kasvoi maaliskuussa selvästi muuta markkinaa nopeammin.
payload.content:
San Franciscon luksusasuntomarkkina on noussut uuteen vauhtiin samaan aikaan, kun tekoäly-yhtiöiden työntekijöille kertynyt varallisuus alkaa näkyä asunto-ostoksina. Redfinin tietojen mukaan kaupungin kalliiden asuntojen myynti kasvoi maaliskuussa 2026 vuodentakaisesta 22,2 prosenttia, kun tavallisempien asuntojen myynti nousi vain 3,8 prosenttia.

## Luksuskauppa vetää muuta markkinaa kovemmin

San Franciscoa ehdittiin viime vuosina pitää esimerkkinä teknologiakaupungista, jonka vetovoima hiipui etätyön ja irtisanomisten myötä. Nyt kehitys näyttää ainakin kalleimmassa päässä toisenlaiselta. Redfinin analyysin mukaan luksusasuntojen kauppa on kasvanut kaksinumeroisesti jo viitenä peräkkäisenä kuukautena.

Ero muuhun asuntomarkkinaan on huomattava. Kun kalliiden asuntojen myynti kasvoi maaliskuussa yli viidenneksen, ei-luksusluokan asuntojen myynti lisääntyi alle neljä prosenttia. Tämä viittaa siihen, että kysyntä ei jakaudu tasaisesti koko markkinaan, vaan painottuu voimakkaasti ostajiin, joilla on poikkeuksellisen vahva maksukyky.

Bay Arean varakkaimmilla postinumeroalueilla asuntojen hinnat ovat nousseet 13,4 prosenttia sen jälkeen, kun GPT-3.5 julkaistiin marraskuussa 2022. Nousu on analyysin mukaan yli kaksinkertainen seuraavaan hintaluokkaan verrattuna.

## Tekoäly-yhtiöiden palkkiot muuttuvat ostovoimaksi

Taustalla on ennen kaikkea San Franciscon ja Piilaakson asema tekoälyalan keskuksena. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind ja joukko raskaasti rahoitettuja kasvuyhtiöitä sijaitsevat lähellä toisiaan, ja kilpailu osaajista on nostanut palkkioita.

Redfin Premier -välittäjä Ali Mafin mukaan alueelle on tullut tekoäly-yhtiöitä, jotka tarjoavat työntekijöilleen erittäin suuria kokonaispalkkioita. Hänen mukaansa osa työntekijöistä saa jopa miljoonan dollarin bonuksia, ja asunnot keräävät kymmeniä tarjouksia. Se on johtanut tilanteisiin, joissa kauppahinta nousee satojatuhansia dollareita pyyntihinnan yli.

Kehitys muistuttaa osin vuoden 2020 ostoryntäystä, mutta sillä on eri painopiste. Pandemian aikana matalat korot nostivat hintoja laajasti eri segmenteissä. Nyt nousua näyttää vetävän ennen kaikkea tekoälyalan synnyttämä uusi varallisuus ja sen keskittyminen aivan markkinan yläpäähän.
summary_bullets: San Franciscon luksusasuntojen myynti kasvoi maaliskuussa 2026 Redfinin mukaan 22,2 prosenttia vuodentakaisesta.
Ei-luksusluokan asuntojen myynti kasvoi samaan aikaan 3,8 prosenttia.
Tekoäly-yhtiöiden suuret palkkiot ja bonukset näkyvät kalliiden asuntojen kysynnässä.

By contrast, non-luxury sales rose just 3.8%, underscoring a widening gap in demand.

San Francisco was written off as tech workers were laid off and remote work became the norm. Then came the robots — and with them, a real estate revival nobody saw coming. Since OpenAI unleashed GPT-3.5 on the world in November 2022, home prices in the Bay Area’s wealthiest ZIP codes have rocketed 13.4%, more than twice the gains posted by the next tier down, according to a Redfin analysis. The city that skeptics were eulogizing is suddenly one of the hottest luxury property markets in the country. The engine behind it is simple: artificial intelligence has become the most lucrative industry on Earth, and its heart beats in Silicon Valley. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind and a wave of heavily-backed startups are all headquartered within miles of each other, and they are paying their talent accordingly.

Redfin Premier agent Ali Mafi has watched the frenzy up close. “There has been an influx of AI companies opening up shop and they’re giving employees giant compensation packages,” he said. “Some people are getting $1 million bonuses. Homes are getting dozens of offers, which is driving up prices and causing many to sell for hundreds of thousands of dollars over the list price. It’s reminiscent of 2020.” That comparison to the pandemic buying frenzy is telling. Back then, rock-bottom mortgage rates sent prices soaring uniformly across all price points, with gains running close to 20% across every market segment.
